reading.title: Cognitive Load Theory and Memory Limitations
reading.passage: Cognitive load theory, proposed by psychologist John Sweller in the 1980s, explains how the human mind processes and retains information. The theory posits that working memory has a limited capacity, typically able to hold only five to nine pieces of information simultaneously. When educational materials or tasks exceed this capacity, learners experience cognitive overload, which significantly impairs their ability to encode information into long-term memory. Research has demonstrated that excessive cognitive load leads to decreased performance and retention rates. For instance, students learning complex mathematical procedures while simultaneously memorizing formulas experience greater difficulty than those who focus on one task at a time. Instructional designers now apply cognitive load theory to create more effective learning environments. By reducing extraneous information, organizing content hierarchically, and breaking complex tasks into manageable segments, educators can facilitate better information processing. Furthermore, multimedia principles derived from this theory suggest that combining verbal and visual information optimally enhances comprehension. Understanding these principles has revolutionized educational psychology, making learning more efficient and accessible across diverse populations.

questions.q: According to the passage, what is the typical capacity of working memory?
options: Two to four pieces of information
Five to nine pieces of information
Ten to fifteen pieces of information
More than twenty pieces of information
questions.explanation: 지문 첫 번째 문장에서 'working memory has a limited capacity, typically able to hold only five to nine pieces of information simultaneously'라고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about students learning mathematical procedures?
options: They should memorize all formulas before solving problems
They perform better when focusing on one task at a time
Mathematics is too difficult for most learners
Cognitive load theory does not apply to mathematics
questions.explanation: 지문에서 '학생들이 수학 절차를 배우면서 동시에 공식을 암기할 때 더 어려움을 경험한다'고 했으므로, 한 번에 한 과제에 집중할 때 더 잘 수행한다는 것을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.q: The word 'impairs' in the first paragraph is closest in meaning to
options: improves
damages or weakens
explains
supports
questions.explanation: 'impairs'는 '손상하다' 또는 '저해하다'라는 뜻으로, 이 맥락에서는 인지 과부하가 기억력을 '약하게 한다'는 의미입니다.

questions.q: Why does the author mention the example of students learning mathematical procedures?
options: To criticize mathematics education
To illustrate the negative effects of excessive cognitive load
To suggest that formulas are unnecessary
To prove that cognitive load theory is incorrect
questions.explanation: 저자는 이 예시를 통해 인지 과부하가 실제로 학습 능력에 부정적인 영향을 미친다는 것을 구체적으로 보여주고 있습니다.

sentences.original: When educational materials or tasks exceed this capacity, learners experience cognitive overload, which significantly impairs their ability to encode information into long-term memory.
sentences.paraphrase: The capacity to absorb educational content is substantially damaged when individuals are presented with materials or assignments that surpass their cognitive capabilities, resulting in overload.
sentences.tip: 원인-결과 구조 유지하면서 능동태→수동태로 변환하고, 'exceed'를 'surpass'로 동의어 치환함

sentences.original: Instructional designers now apply cognitive load theory to create more effective learning environments.
sentences.paraphrase: Contemporary educational professionals utilize principles of cognitive load theory in designing learning spaces that enhance instructional effectiveness.
sentences.tip: 동사구 'apply ~ to create'를 명사구 'utilize ~ in designing'으로 재구성하여 표현 다양화

sentences.original: By reducing extraneous information, organizing content hierarchically, and breaking complex tasks into manageable segments, educators can facilitate better information processing.
sentences.paraphrase: Educators achieve improved information processing when they remove unnecessary details, arrange material in sequential order, and divide complicated assignments into smaller portions.
sentences.tip: 병렬 구조의 전치사구를 절 구조로 재구성하고, 'extraneous'를 'unnecessary'로 단순화

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer spending more time with friends. Others prefer spending more time with family. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details.
model_sentences: I definitely prefer spending more time with my family because family relationships form the foundation of my life.
First, my family provides unconditional support during difficult times, which friends sometimes cannot offer to the same extent.
For example, when I failed my college entrance exam, my parents encouraged me and helped me prepare for the next attempt without judgment.
Additionally, family bonds are permanent and irreplaceable, whereas friendships can change as we move or enter different life stages.
In conclusion, while friends are important for social development, family is the most essential relationship to prioritize in my life.

listening.title: 경제학 강의: 공급과 수요의 기본 원리
listening.script: Professor: Today, we're going to discuss one of the most fundamental concepts in economics: supply and demand. The law of demand states that when the price of a good increases, the quantity demanded by consumers decreases, assuming all other factors remain constant. Conversely, the law of supply indicates that when prices rise, suppliers are willing to produce more goods. Now, let's consider a practical example. Imagine the price of coffee increases dramatically. What happens? First, consumers reduce their coffee purchases because it becomes more expensive. Simultaneously, coffee producers see higher profits and increase production. Eventually, these two forces interact at what we call the equilibrium point, where the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded. At this point, the market clears, and there's no tendency for prices to change further. This fundamental principle explains price fluctuations in virtually every market, from housing to technology. Understanding supply and demand helps us predict market behavior and make informed economic decisions.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the lecture?
options: The history of coffee prices
How supply and demand determine market prices
Methods for increasing consumer spending
Strategies for producers to reduce costs
questions.explanation: 교수는 경제학의 기본 개념인 공급과 수요에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 이것이 강의의 주요 주제입니다.

questions.q: According to the professor, what happens at the equilibrium point?
options: Consumers stop buying products
Producers stop making goods
The quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded
Prices increase indefinitely
questions.explanation: 교수가 명시적으로 '균형점에서 공급량과 수요량이 같다'고 설명했습니다.

questions.q: Why does the professor use coffee as an example?
options: To show that coffee is the most important commodity
To illustrate how supply and demand principles work in a practical market situation
To argue that coffee prices are too high
To demonstrate that producers always make profits
questions.explanation: 교수는 커피 가격 상승이라는 구체적인 예시를 통해 공급과 수요의 원리가 실제로 어떻게 작동하는지 설명하고 있습니다.
